document.title: The context-audit guide ("Anthropic deleted 80% of its own instructions") — the deletion discipline our review cycle was missing

body.text:
# The context-audit guide ("Anthropic deleted 80% of its own instructions") — the deletion discipline our review cycle was missing
Source: x.com/free_ai_guides/status/2082463119742320825 (read 2026-07-30, 21K views; grounded in Anthropic's published context-engineering direction — the "unhobbling" framing, Chroma's context-rot research, Manus's tool-sprawl finding. The 80%-cut figure is reported-not-independently-verified; fine for internal use, gets a source check before ever appearing in content).
**Why this one matters more than most content links: it describes OUR corpus.** A year of small corrections that only ever grows, rules written months apart quietly arguing, doctrine sprawl (already flagged in addendum §G) — the CARR instruction estate is the article's patient. We HAVE the scheduled audit (monthly playbook review + size sweep, the 15th); what it lacked was a deletion METHOD. Adopted:
1. **The Delete Test → the playbook review's per-rule checklist (4 questions):** still true (or written for an older model)? · conflicts with anything in ANY layer? · would a competent new hire need telling? · name the specific failure it prevents — can't name it, not load-bearing. Cut on any yes/fail. Obvious cuts + dead conflicts go immediately; suspected obsolete workarounds get pulled for a week, restored if quality drops.
2. **A mechanical CONFLICTS PASS joins the review:** the teaching layer's conflict detection (built for teacher-vs-teacher) extends to the whole compiled corpus — every review runs a contradiction sweep across doctrine + rules + skills, because conflicts cost more than length and are invisible to the author ("you wrote both; both looked reasonable on the day").
3. **Workaround-vs-preference split, and the migration named for what it is:** many standing rules are workarounds for limits the record layer DELETES (hand-edit bans, guarded writers, ledger claims, propagation passes) — the "what dissolves" list is an UNHOBBLING, the article's word, and post-migration reviews must keep asking "is this rule compensating for a limitation that no longer exists?" Preferences stay; scaffolding goes.
4. **Rules → outcomes in the context compiler (Wave 4 principle):** compiled context prefers destination-descriptions over process rules (their example: "write code that reads like the surrounding code" replacing a rule list). Pairs with the smallest-high-signal-set doctrine already adopted.
5. **THE GUARD, non-negotiable, written into the review checklist:** safety, permission, and gate constraints are NEVER audit targets — the one human gate, no-fabrication, placeholder rules, confidentiality, consent rules stay explicit forever regardless of model capability. The article says this itself; our version is stronger: an audit that proposes cutting a gate has failed the audit.
7. **Timing rule:** the freshly-built record layer is EXEMPT (their "setup you built last week" exclusion) — the audit targets the accumulated pre-migration corpus, at the Wave 4 compile and every review after.
**Content note:** "we deleted half our own rulebook and nothing broke" is a strong future chapter of the philosophy story — the system that prunes itself is rarer than the system that grows.

1. **Conflict Finder:** editor persona; find every pair of instructions that could pull toward different actions on the same task; quote both, describe the collision situation, say which was meant to win; list redundant pairs; name THE one conflict to resolve first. Resolve by DELETING the unmeant half — never add a third rule to settle an argument.
4. **Rules→Outcome:** technical-writer persona; infer the result the process rules wanted; describe the destination as what the output looks like / must contain / what would make it wrong; safety-permission-legal-accuracy constraints stay explicit; unclear rules listed as questions, never silently dropped.

document.title: Claude native context and token efficiency design

body.text: Keep native history append-only and keep system and tool configuration stable within a task. New corrections arrive as new turns; never rewrite old turns or reinsert thinking blocks. Retrieve specific record facts and bounded source excerpts on demand. Do not repeat unchanged boot packs each turn or run a separate model summary after every tool. Mid-conversation additionalContext is appended after the existing cached prefix, so the prior prefix can still hit while the injected text permanently grows the window. Candidate additionalContext is tagged so the transcript can measure its UTF-8 bytes per event, per tool call, and per session; the acceptance run counts all hook-injected context, including existing rule-delivery hooks. Begin the candidate adapter in shadow mode and use an explicit repository/task/event selector as the only lever that enables injection. Batch bounded tool outputs and delegate independent noisy work only when the returned summary saves more context than it costs. Cache hits reduce processing price but do not shrink the context window or prove reasoning quality. As a separate measured hypothesis on Claude Code 2.1.260 or later, compare a fixed tool set with deferred MCP schema loading and check statusline prompt_cache.last_miss_cause for tools_changed; use the result to decide tool-loading order, never an assumption.

Retain Claude Code's native context capacity, cache duration, and auto-compaction defaults for the baseline and whenever evidence is missing or a candidate fails acceptance. Read the effective context_window_size and used_percentage from a version-qualified statusline sample after an API response; do not infer capacity from a transcript, model name, account label, or invocation count. Treat null fields as unknown. On 2.1.251 or later, record SessionStart resume/fork seconds_since_last_response, context_tokens, prompt_cache_likely_expired, and estimated_cache_write_usd when present, and statusline prompt_cache warm, ttl, expires_at, hit_ratio, misses, and recache_tokens_if_cold. On 2.1.260 or later, record diagnosed miss causes. Keep these observations separate from billed usage. Do not set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT globally. The percentage override can only lower the threshold. The token-window variable accepts 100000 through 1000000, is capped by the model window, and outranks /autocompact, --autocompact, and autoCompactWindow. Later per-workload experiments use the per-launch --autocompact surface first, with model, plan, provider, effective statusline window, and all three environment variables captured. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT forces native-1M models to 200K behavior. One-million-token availability varies by model, provider, plan, and disablement; never assume it from the model family. No percentage automatically resets, clears, forks, or hands off a task.

The recovery pack orders objective, latest correction, binding, next action, and stale-state warning first, followed by unresolved decisions and verified artifacts. Cap the complete additionalContext string, including headings and warnings, at 8000 UTF-8 bytes. This deliberately stays below Claude Code's 10000-character hook-output limit, leaves framing margin for multibyte text, and is smaller than the Codex adapter's 12000-byte cap because the Claude design must coexist with measured existing hook injection. Render whole typed fields only; never cut UTF-8, JSON, a constraint, or an action halfway. On overflow, omit lower-priority whole items, print exact omitted counts by class, and include bounded record/source retrieval references. The cap limits added recovery text, not native history. Every hook input supplies transcript_path: canonicalize and open only that exact supplied path, require it inside the trusted current Claude transcript root, reject symlinks, compare the opened file identity to validated metadata before every read, and refuse alternate discovery paths, Codex payloads, cross-owner data, rotation, replacement, or truncation. Parsing is version-tested, local, read-only, byte/line/result bounded, and allowlists recognized Claude row shapes. Store no raw transcript copy. A record outage leaves native Claude operation and native defaults running but emits an explicit incomplete-state warning when the event can deliver context; it never invents a checkpoint or silently labels coverage fresh.

Before any Claude activation, separately review and remediate the existing hooks/context-handoff-gate.py and ops/config/session-context-lifecycle.v1.json collision. The manifest currently lacks claude-fable-5-1 and can fall to invocation caps that demand a successor far before native auto-compaction. The remediation must add the exact probed model identity and window only after verification, make the supported statusline context window authoritative, and prevent the gate's 70 percent line or invocation fallback from blocking Stop or forcing a handoff while native compaction is healthy. With a missing or invalid capacity signal it may record and announce unknown state, but it must not infer exhaustion from call count. Explicit user handoff, verified terminal failure, and true recovery remain separate paths. Claude continuity stays disabled until collision fixtures prove this precedence; this doctrine does not change the gate itself.

Run at least 30 paired tasks: the same ten code, ten debug, and ten research tasks under native-default baseline and candidate, with fixed inputs, model/provider/account, repository state, and declared warm-cache, cold-resume, repeated-compaction, and interrupted-operation strata. Predeclare the score and rate table. Primary gates are verified completion for every task, zero lost user corrections, zero duplicate side effects/actions, zero cross-task/owner/runtime leakage, exact fork/root/subagent isolation, and verified native additionalContext delivery. Candidate wins only if all primary gates hold, aggregate total model cost or aggregate end-to-end latency improves by at least 10 percent, and every other predeclared quality/cost/latency guardrail regresses by no more than 5 percent. These margins are proposals, not measured results. Any failed gate, unavailable winning measure, or inconclusive comparison keeps native defaults.

Use transcript assistant usage as the task-local accounting source: deduplicate rows by a version-tested stable response/message/request identity, then sum input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, and cache_creation_input_tokens separately across unique responses; retain ephemeral_5m and ephemeral_1h cache-creation splits when exposed, and price each category with the frozen provider/model rates. Never sum statusline current_usage snapshots as session usage. Mark compaction sampling cost unknown unless a distinct transcript/API usage row exposes it. Statusline supplies effective window and, from 2.1.251, main-conversation cache state; it excludes subagent cache statistics. Optional OpenTelemetry may corroborate claude_code.token.usage types input, output, cacheRead, cacheCreation and api_request cache fields, with prompt/tool-content logging disabled; it is not required for task-local truth. Measure tagged hook-injected UTF-8 bytes per event, tool call, and session from the transcript, stale checkpoints, CAS conflicts, idempotence, and selector behavior. On 2.1.260 or later, test whether deferred MCP schema loading causes tools_changed. Values unavailable before or during the run remain explicitly unknown.

body.text: Separate pure pack rendering, authenticated record access, Claude identity/transcript parsing, metric collection, and hook protocol. Do not rely on Claude Code's defaults of 600 seconds for most synchronous command hooks and 30 seconds for UserPromptSubmit. The initial synchronous continuity-hook proposal uses a 10-second configured hook timeout and one 8-second internal event deadline. Recovery/read receives at most five seconds; rendering is local and bounded; the attempt receipt is written after rendering and before stdout, with a bounded call that ends by second seven; stdout completes by second eight. The receipt records configured timeout, internal deadline, rendered digest/bytes, whether the receipt write completed, and injection_attempted=true only when rendering succeeded and the completed receipt precedes printing. If the receipt write fails, delivered context carries an outage warning where supported and no durable receipt claims delivery. A Claude timeout discards output, so timeout is never evidence of delivery. PreCompact and PostCompact print no user/context fields and never block. SessionEnd uses a 5-second configured timeout and a 3-second internal deadline and is not the sole enforcement for clear. All network retries share the one deadline; no per-call timeout may restart it. Bound stdout and emit at most one warning per event. A native smoke must prove model-visible delivery before activation; receipts alone prove only ordered attempts. No local prose-cache fallback. The future backend interface is checkpoint CAS, bounded recovery read, immutable lifecycle/source receipts, explicit task declaration/takeover, and runtime-specific authorization, with registry migration independently reviewed before wiring.

This section contains durable change-control rules, not a queue journal. Model Room delivery, task ids, generation numbers, implementation progress, and reviewer status belong in loop, decision, or review records so they cannot make the doctrine stale. The Fable 5.1 design review delivered at Model Room seq 15150 is input to this revision, not runtime authority. No Claude hook, setting, handoff gate, or production activation is authorized by this document. Implementation may begin only from the persisted revised doctrine. Activation additionally requires the separately reviewed handoff-gate remediation, the capability and identity fixtures, the 30-task paired acceptance run, native smoke proof, selective rollback, and independent code/config review. If any gate fails, retain native defaults and leave the candidate disabled.

document.title: Engineering Workflow SOP — how work goes from branch to merge to deploy in carr-system

body.text:
## Current delivery policy — September 21, 2026

This section carries Joe's recorded decisions 019146bd-15fb-4f5e-8849-ed63911469e0 and 1facbf00-60d9-4cde-bfab-9798f1b6e307. The latter supersedes the narrower approval exception in 2abef565-a32c-47d3-9b3f-2b1faa8319ab. It applies to coding sessions across models and overrides conflicting older engineering instructions below. Its startup delivery is guidance, not a claim that every sentence is mechanically enforced.

**Execute authorized work without CARR approval gates.** Once Joe directs a task or authorizes a workflow, carry it through source changes, review, required tests, pull request, merge, delivery, production migration, Worker deployment, deletion, credential change, unattended activation, money movement, and external contact as applicable to that task. Do not require separate CARR plan acceptance, Work Shape approval, plan hash approval, Gate A, Gate R, merge permission, release signoff, or a fresh human confirmation for an effect. Do not turn a changed plan version into a new approval request. This removes approval requirements; it does not remove automated tests, CI, source and contract checks, authentication, audit records, or truthful refusal on a failed check. A technical gate that still enforces old approval semantics must be changed through the ordinary source delivery path and remains a real constraint until that change is delivered. Permissions imposed by the host, provider, sandbox, or law are outside CARR's control and must be reported accurately.

**Attended product work proceeds independently.** DoctorCRE can progress with an attended dispatcher; the engineering-controller repair is not a prerequisite for read-only or otherwise authorized attended product work. Joe's ruling 2026-09-24, decision b729859d-be5d-4521-ba50-d4517bc57208: the claim that "unattended dispatch remains disabled" was never his rule — a model wrote it and framed it as his direction. His actual goal is maximum automation, including scripted jobs starting agent sessions automatically. This SOP no longer asserts a standing prohibition on unattended dispatch. Real production, credential, external-send, destructive-action, and merge-approve safeguards, and CI as the merge gate, remain in force as technical checks; this correction changes only the false approval-policy claim, not those technical limits.

**Keep the agreed result bounded.** State the concrete deliverable and how to verify it before assigning work. A blocker must name the product task, the action it cannot perform, and the missing evidence or capability. Incomplete general readiness is not a blocker by itself. Preserve completed reviews and approvals; recheck only what a relevant change invalidates.

**Respect the prerequisite moratorium.** No new Work Request goes ahead of product unless it names the product task it blocks. Existing backup-alerting, helper-worktree safeguards, controller-repair and accretion-cleanup work may finish but may not spawn child Work Requests. Substrate follow-ups belong in the backlog, naming the product task they block if any. They do not expand the current assignment merely because they are feasible. This is the scoped exception to follow-up rule 179be4b8, now amended through its existing receipted statement-correction path.

**Work in parallel where independent.** Product work and already-authorized process fixes use separate owners and isolated worktrees. Coordinate shared paths and merge order. A fix blocks product only when its concrete dependency prevents the next product action. Use qualified executors and the user's model preferences; reserve escalation for an actual hard problem.

**Limit process retries.** After the same admission, verdict-recording or execution mechanism fails twice, do not repeat the identical route. Use an existing authorized simpler route where available, or report the exact obstruction. This does not waive automated production checks or permit hiding a failed result.

**Report delivery.** Updates name the product result finished, the task being worked on, and any concrete blocker. Process optimization remains bounded work alongside the build. Do not turn simplification into another prerequisite program.

**Local feedback and hosted verification.** Joe reopened the September 2 full-local-suite cost ruling: fast pre-push feedback, targeting about one minute, and full required hosted CI are the intended route. Measure actual duration; do not claim the target is achieved until verified. Run appropriate local tests while implementing, without automatically rerunning the full suite on every push. No skip variable, secret-check removal, inherited-Git-environment shortcut, timeout inflation or weakened assertion is authorized.

Historical September 2 rationale and measurements follow for provenance; conflicting requirements are superseded by the current policy above.

# Engineering Workflow SOP

**Historical scope:** the September 2, 2026 engineering SOP; current delivery policy above controls conflicting instructions.

**Provenance.** Joe's ruling of 2026-09-02 after the September Actions census: a two-partner system in its build phase does not pay hundreds of dollars a month so the cloud can run tests a laptop runs in minutes, and the fleet stops using GitHub as its test runner. His words: "are you being excessive and wasteful of action minutes and being lazy instead of just debugging code before its ready?" The measured answer was yes. Over 2026-09-01 and 02: 12 of 25 branches were red on their first push; branches averaged 4.1 pushes to merge, one took 14; 25 of 32 red CI runs came from one hard-coded test count; successful CI runs went from 4.3 minutes in mid-August to 19.6 minutes on September 1 and the response was raising the timeout; 2,911 of the month's 3,000 included minutes were gone by day two.

**What was researched.** Each rule below was checked against how experienced teams actually operate (Google's engineering practices, trunk-based development, GitHub's own documentation, practitioner discussion at volume) before it was written. Where the industry has no settled convention the rule says so and gives our measured number instead.

**What this SOP owns.** The day-to-day loop: branch, build, prove locally, open a pull request, merge, and the CI, test, migration, and public-repo hygiene around it.

**What it does not own.** The canonical checkout's freshness, branch deletion law, janitors, frozen installs, hook resolution, and runtime isolation belong to the Repo Hygiene Program build plan (Clean Tree operating model) and are not restated here. Production database operations belong to the Neon Database SOP. Worker releases, rollback, and R2 belong to the Cloudflare Edge SOP. The rule that ci.sh is the one check script and that neither the workflow nor the hook may carry check logic stands unchanged.

**How to read it.** Every section gives a decision procedure, meaning ordered questions with a checkable answer, and names the audit signal that shows the rule was skipped. A rule with no audit signal is a suggestion, and suggestions are what this SOP replaces.

body.text:
## 14. Jev System One architecture, evaluation, and control boundaries

Joe approved these requirements on 2026-09-20 with “okay well do it.” Canonical decision: `4632ff74-526c-456b-83dc-1fd90e56f766`; decision event: `ad3ee042-c84b-4b68-9a6f-3f9727f1ce86`. They extend the existing ruling that Jev is the default decision layer for qualified judgment-shaped work across CARR (`7b0d1353-4056-45f1-8d2f-011b76a51508`).

### Authority boundary

Jev supplies narrow typed judgments and probabilities over explicit evidence and candidate sets. Deterministic code owns identity, tenancy, authority, permissions, arithmetic, dates and counts, invariants, policy enforcement, execution, writes, state transitions, hard gates, retries, and proof of completion. Confidence is evidence for a decision; it is never permission, correctness, or completion by itself. A Jev or general-LLM failure must remain visible and must not silently become an affirmative judgment.

### Approved requirements

1. **Jev-as-judge evaluation fabric.** Evaluate fixed, source-bound agent traces with atomic typed questions covering correctness, groundedness, usefulness, retrieval, tool use, drift, and completion. Calibrate against human-labeled oracle cases, including ambiguity and no-valid-answer cases. Measure accuracy separately from repeatability and variance. Bind model, question, state, and source digests; record latency and cost. Judgments act from the start (see Acting from day one below). Prefer binary checks and separate binary subchecks to vague Likert scores. Low cost or low variance does not excuse a consistently wrong judge.

2. **Jev-first orchestration.** Deterministic workflows collect evidence, enumerate currently valid candidates, own policy, and execute effects. Jev decides bounded semantic questions such as routing, whether a more expensive model is needed, and the smallest relevant context or option set. An open-ended LLM fallback is explicitly unverified and cannot claim completion.

3. **Independent worker supervision.** A Jev supervisor may assess the original job, worker output, Git changes, tests, and prior assessments for stuckness, drift, evidence sufficiency, and completion likelihood. Only the deterministic controller may continue, steer, stop, retry, verify, finish, or escalate work.

4. **Tool-result and retrieved-context screening.** Before untrusted tool descriptions, calls, results, or retrieved context reach an agent, use bounded semantic checks for prompt injection, misleading authority claims, relevance, and other identified risks. Deterministic permission, provenance, tenant-isolation, and taint gates remain hard boundaries.

5. **Universal judgment contracts.** Every production judgment contract provides an explicit abstention state such as `abstain`, `cannot_tell`, or `unavailable`; risk-specific confidence bands; call, question, token, and time budgets; state, question, source, and model provenance; and a fresh external readback after any action whose result matters. Instructions belong in the typed questions, not in hidden assumptions.

6. **Application-level, scope-first placement.** Do not make Jev calls inside SQL or Postgres the default architecture. First apply deterministic tenant and authority scope, then provide Jev a bounded shortlist at the application or service layer. This keeps credentials, caching, timeouts, budgets, receipts, and failure behavior explicit. A database placement requires a separately justified exception with equivalent boundaries and evidence.

### Acting from day one (2026-09-24 ruling)

Joe ruled on 2026-09-24: “we need to just act now. forget the shadow period” (decision `5ec806a4-e4bf-41cf-a3d0-59f37432b0e2`). No Jev judgment waits for a shadow period or pre-action human-oracle calibration before it may influence control flow. Joe confirmed the scope the same day: “no i also mean every jev check in the system too is not a shadow.” The Jev-steered Flash script harness and its pre-flight router (answer directly, write a script, or escalate to Opus or Sol) are still in their testing phase, where the design, kinks and bugs are worked out with Jev auditing and reviewing each harness revision; they go live acting as soon as that phase is complete, with no shadow run between. Each acting use still names its threshold (calibrated on known cases where any exist, a stated starting value where none do), abstention path, deterministic fallback and budget, and keeps its decision log as a replayable audit; a sampled audit of the decisions Jev closed replaces the pre-action shadow period, and a check the audit shows doing harm is pulled back. The authority boundary above is unchanged: deterministic code still owns identity, authority, permissions, arithmetic, writes, execution and proof of completion, and a Jev outage falls back visibly and never becomes an affirmative judgment. The Stop-gate rationing ruling of 2026-08-23 (only the core conduct, completion-evidence and drift-assertion hooks may reopen a turn) is separate and unchanged: an acting Jev check on a Stop hook announces rather than reopening the turn unless it is one of those three.

### Rollout and proof

Adopt these requirements through eligible product-attached slices under the current product-first policy; they do not authorize a parallel substrate program or widen an active Work Request. A control-affecting use must name its threshold, abstention path, deterministic fallback, budget, model/version binding, fixtures, and measurable success and failure criteria.

Current delivered bindings are limited to semantic rule selection in PR 1095 and automatic build-turn/post-write advisory review in PR 1096. Those deliveries do not establish that all six requirements are implemented. `WR-000123` records the DoctorCRE Needs Joe advisory-prioritization gap. Further implementation must use the authorized repository, ordinary source-review path, and effect-specific approvals. This section is architecture doctrine, not release, deployment, production-migration, unattended-run, or destructive-action authority.

### Research provenance

The approved synthesis was derived from Joe’s six supplied practitioner posts and checked against TypeSafe Jev documentation, LangChain’s Jev harness and agent-evaluation reports, the maintained Stanley repository, and Hamel Husain’s binary-evaluation guidance. Research establishes the design rationale; CARR-owned calibration and delivery evidence establish whether each implementation works here.

### September 21 extension: Jev-aware harness and Model Room

Joe asked to carry the substantive capabilities from Diogo Almeida's coding-agent notes and the linked 0xMovez synthesis into the system build, and to put Jev into Model Room routing. Decision `7d86e17e-4dd3-424f-be35-d525a1882be2` records that direction. This extends requirements 1–6 through their existing owners; it does not create a second agent platform or change an immutable accepted Work Request plan.

7. **Explicit, reconstructible state and query-aware context.** Address relevant user turns, source reads, tool inputs and outputs, diffs, tests, rules, and prior decisions as source-bound chunks. For the current question, choose hide, short, long, or full visibility under a token budget. Preserve an exact path back to the source, authority-bearing context, corrections, and unresolved evidence. Evaluate whether a smaller pack omitted a needed fact, especially an exact instruction, correction, source, or unresolved exception. Measure false drops, omission regret, and added latency against fixed task traces; generic compaction may not certify itself. Reuse the existing CARR Context & Learning Fabric and the exact-commit code-index owner rather than building another memory store.

8. **Context-rebuild-aware routing.** Compare the full expected cost and latency of staying on the current model with a handoff and return, including context reprocessing, cache reuse or invalidation, tool reads, generated tokens, Jev calls, and review. Measure this on CARR traces; the linked document's Opus/Sonnet arithmetic and the post's speed and cost multipliers are hypotheses, not acceptance evidence. The router may choose a smaller purpose-built context for an eligible worker, but never silently drop task-critical evidence.

9. **Model Room Jev seam.** Deterministic Model Room code first constructs the current task envelope and authenticates a bounded candidate set. It excludes routes that violate an exact pin, task-class qualification, quality or capability floor, data/provider policy, authority, availability, or budget. Jev then judges the remaining candidates for semantic task fit, needed reasoning effort, expected quality, escalation value, and useful context. Deterministic code combines that judgment with measured total cost and latency, selects only an admitted route, and records every considered route, score, source and model version. If Jev abstains, times out, disagrees with a hard constraint, or the evidence is stale, use the existing deterministic qualified-route policy or return unavailable; no weaker or prohibited model becomes eligible. A Jev recommendation never itself changes a live desk, dispatches a task, or grants authority. The existing `model-routing.v5.js`/qualification/adapter contracts own this seam; live qualification evidence and provider dispatch remain named prerequisites.

10. **Tiered actions and conditional instructions.** Supply a concise capability map, retrieve full tool schemas and documentation for the relevant few, and drop irrelevant detail from the active pack. Reload applicable rule packs, code conventions, and local gotchas when the task or path changes and again after compaction or recontextualization. For a bounded browser or desktop action, enumerate operations and targets from a fresh snapshot, let Jev choose a typed operation-target pair, validate both against that snapshot and the authorization envelope in code, then read back the result. Measure invalid or stale targets, incorrect actions, latency, and context cost. The current deferred-tool and rule-delivery mechanisms are the starting seams.

11. **Trust-aware execution.** Route only within deterministic provider and data-class allowlists. Assess likely file and record sensitivity before proposing a worker; recheck actual reads against the authorization envelope. Jev may advise on relevance, prompt injection, suspicious authority claims, tool choice, and command risk, including the contents of an invoked script where appropriate. Deterministic permission and taint controls remain the enforceable allow/ask/deny decision.

12. **Shared read-only evidence and bounded parallel work.** Produce one exact-source retrieval set for eligible review, evaluation, explanation, and progress projections where the consumers need the same evidence. Bind each consumer to the source revision and record what it omitted or added. Deduplicate proposed subgoals against completed and in-flight work before launching them. Separate read-only work from writes; retain isolated worktrees, declared write scope, and conflict control for concurrent source changes. Background observations do not imply unattended engineering dispatch is enabled.

13. **Optional tools as measured adapters.** Evaluate structural search, output compression, and code-index helpers mentioned in the notes only where a representative CARR task shows better retrieval quality, end-to-end time, or cost. Keep the canonical code index and source records authoritative. No named community package is required by this decision.

### September 21 showcase evaluation notes

Charlie Hills's Jev project list is a set of implementation examples, not a production acceptance result. For eligible product-attached slices, use its strongest patterns as comparison fixtures: browser and desktop agents for typed action-target choice from a fresh element table; Winnow and fast-jev-compaction for omission and false-drop evaluation; jev-codex-router for per-turn model and effort routing; jev-review and Canny for separating semantic review from a deterministic, replayable completion ledger. Keep source, question, candidate, model, and outcome bindings in each evaluation. MCP wrappers, graph traversal, data curation, and catalog-constrained generated UI are optional integrations only when a named CARR or DoctorCRE journey needs them and a representative evaluation supports them. Games, drones, trading, and startup scoring establish no CARR requirement. Do not install a community package merely because it appears in the list.

### Model Room rollout proof

Jev rankings select among the authenticated candidate set from the start; the deterministic selected route is recorded beside each choice for the audit. Use human-labeled task classes and actual completed-task outcomes to compare route quality, wrong-route rate, abstention, quality-floor breaches, total cost, latency, provider failures, and context omissions. Separate initial routing from mid-task rerouting; a handoff is charged for rebuilding context and re-reading the returned evidence. Each task class carries a versioned threshold, exact model and question binding, budget, fallback, and a sampled independent audit; a class whose audit shows a negative result is pulled back to the deterministic route. Explicit user or accepted-plan model pins remain exact. No architecture claim says Jev can always pick the right model; the product goal is a measurably better selection with visible uncertainty and no loss of hard guarantees.

### Placement and sequencing

CARR owns Model Room policy, qualifications, routing decisions, authority, business context, and product-runtime contracts. DoctorCRE displays permitted route and uncertainty evidence. The software factory may own exact-commit code retrieval and read-only development adapters; products do not depend on it at runtime. Attach implementation to the next eligible DoctorCRE journey or already-accepted owner slice. The context and learning extension stays under WR-000013; this section grants no new Work Request precedence, source lease, migration, release, unattended execution, or provider-routing activation.

Additional source provenance: [Diogo Almeida design notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1G61uUB0FifUnmmrPzFQojZ3KpczYKmXGpgEXDJ2l_Zg/mobilebasic), [0xMovez synthesis](https://x.com/0xmovez/status/2102049863449858053), and its [derived PDF](https://drive.google.com/file/d/17h982xvsL3E7b80iGmOCfKp9qTOW9ohv/view). The original is a design note; the post and PDF are derivative, and none establishes CARR performance.

document.title: Rule delivery: the three load layers, and the gate that keeps them honest

body.text:
WHAT THIS IS. Three load layers deciding WHEN a taught rule's text reaches a session, which is a different question from how the rule is enforced. layer0 is recited at every boot and holds only what binds regardless of task. control means an installed deny, stop or schema gate prints the rule at the moment it binds, so boot recitation adds nothing. pack means the rule arrives when the session's OBSERVED WORK matches a pack trigger.

WHY IT EXISTS. Until 2026-08-23 the loader had one mode: recite every active rule into every session, whatever that session turned out to be doing. That is a standing violation of the core-routing rule, which says the always-read core holds only what every session needs regardless of task, and the violating thing was the boot verb itself. The enforcement recategorization shipped into production the same morning and changed none of it, because enforcement and delivery are different axes and only one of them had ever been tagged.

WHAT THE 2026-08-23 COUNCIL RULED, both chairs independently and in the same shape. Layer 0 is small, targeted at 35 shared rules or fewer plus the partner's own always-on set. A null workflow returns Layer 0, never all 204 and never nothing. The boot payload carries a PACK INDEX - pack names and what triggers each - so an undeclared session can see what it has not loaded. And one chair named the failure to avoid in words worth keeping: do not flip applicability on with wildcard tags and call it scoping, because that would silently drop rules on undeclared sessions, which is the exact failure the session-name rule was taught to prevent.

WHERE EACH PIECE LIVES. The reviewed tags are in ops/config/rule-enforcement-map.json, the same file the enforcement half is reviewed in, under rule_load_layers and rule_packs. ops/rule-load-layer-check.py holds the contract statically and refuses a wildcard pack, an untagged active rule, a control tag on a rule nothing can refuse, and a Layer 0 over its cap. Migration 0288 gives the tags a home in the database with the same refusals as constraints, plus ops.rule_delivery_plan, which is the delivery selector. bin/sync-rule-admission-prod.sh installs both halves through one door. hooks/rule-pack-drift-gate.py is the Stop gate. ops/rule-delivery-shadow-watch.py is the nightly comparison.

THE SELECTOR IS NOT ops.applicable_rules, AND THIS IS THE TRAP TO REMEMBER. Migration 0228 replaced that function with a receipt-bound enforcement compiler: a rule comes back only while its statement hash, normalized contract, authority receipt and every installed control still match an immutable approval. Measured against production on 2026-08-23 it returned ONE row out of 218 admitted rules, with no filter at all. It is correct as an enforcement compiler and catastrophic as a delivery selector - a boot that compiled its rules from it would hand the session one rule and call that the applicable set. Anything that needs to know what a session should be handed calls ops.rule_delivery_plan.

THE DRIFT GATE IS WHAT MAKES SCOPING SAFE, not an addition to it. Rule 347a9ca6 says a session's name does not predict the work it will do, taught after Joe pointed out that he does full system builds inside sessions named for routine work. Scoping delivery on a declaration would install that failure rather than merely risk it. So the Stop gate diffs the turn's own tool calls and prose against the packs the session loaded, and in enforced mode reopens the turn naming the missing pack. It judges what the session DID, never what it said it would do, and it reads the session's own calls rather than what tools said back - the boot payload carries every pack's triggers in its index, so a gate that scanned results would demand every pack on every turn.

SHADOW BEFORE ENFORCEMENT, ONE WEEK, and the switch is a database row rather than a deploy. ops.rule_delivery_policy starts in shadow: the selector runs, the payload reports what a scoped boot WOULD have omitted, and the recitation is untouched. The drift gate records instead of blocking. A MISS is the row that matters - a rule this turn's work needed that a scoped boot would not have delivered - and enforcement flips on at zero unexplained misses on consequential actions. Both chairs required this and the reason is that the failure is silent by construction: a session that boots with fewer rules looks exactly like a session that boots correctly.

body.text:
## Current ownership and sequencing — 2026-09-20

Joe approved reconciliation in native task 01a0b013-2734-7bf3-9f4f-db63963ff8a4 ("do it"). WR-000013 and doctrine:runbook#agent-learning-v2 (section 0d3a6481-583f-4b3a-893f-505fd98ddcb4, current revision) are the ONE continuing implementation and amendment home. Its current policy governs retrieval-first delivery, Jev, correction lineage, scope, economics and calibration. Reuse adequate v1 mechanisms and evidence; do not start a separate WR-000009 learning implementation. This is scoped design supersession, not retirement of useful code/evidence or mutation of accepted PLAN-89868a5da5b8-v1. Rebinding affected execution contracts remains required before changed work. The v1 design below is retained as reusable historical baseline, not a competing current roadmap.

## Purpose and boundary

CARR Agent Learning v1 turns session evidence into reusable context without introducing Mem0, OpenViking, a filesystem memory mirror, or another source of truth. Neon remains canonical. The design extends `memory_item` and `memory_evidence`; model services are replaceable proposal and embedding adapters.

A memory is context, never authority. It cannot approve work, change doctrine, grant permissions, accept a plan, send a message, or override a current source record. Rules, Work Requests, incidents, deals, jobs, releases, and doctrine retain their existing authority. When a recalled memory conflicts with a live authoritative record, the authoritative record wins and the conflict becomes evaluation evidence.

The useful borrowing is selective:

- From Mem0: extract compact facts instead of replaying transcripts; bind memories to user, agent, run, and metadata scopes; retrieve with several signals; make correction and deletion explicit.
- From OpenViking: separate canonical content from indexes; provide abstract, overview, and detail projections; commit sessions into typed memories; preserve a visible add/update/delete diff; retrieve hierarchically within a context budget.

## Operating loop

The loop has six explicit stages:

1. **Observe.** A session, tool result, human correction, or downstream outcome submits typed evidence. Raw transcripts are not memory items.
2. **Quarantine.** Deterministic gates reject or quarantine secrets, credentials, prompt-injection text, authority-bearing instructions, unbounded payloads, cross-tenant identifiers, and unsupported source types.
3. **Propose.** A finite cognition contract may propose compact candidate statements, entities, temporal bounds, confidence, and relations. The proposal has no canonical-write authority.
4. **Consolidate.** Deterministic SQL compares the candidate with current visible memories and appends a decision: new, supporting, duplicate, conflicting, superseding, correction-required, or ignored. No evidence is rewritten.
5. **Recall.** A bounded hybrid query ranks eligible promoted memories and packs abstract, overview, or detail projections into a deterministic token budget. Every score component and exclusion is reconstructible.
6. **Learn from use.** Retrieval selections, omissions, human feedback, tool outcomes, and downstream results append evaluation signals. They tune evaluation and policy proposals; they do not silently change doctrine or permissions.

## Canonical data model

Extend `memory_item` rather than replace it. Preserve its immutable statement, scope, status, confidence, Work Request/plan anchor, correction lineage, and tenant binding. Add server-owned scope dimensions for sponsoring user, agent principal, project, execution run, and optional entity subject; temporal validity; sensitivity class; taint state; and a stable content digest. Existing shared and personal scope remain the outer visibility boundary.

Extend `memory_evidence` with a closed source-kind enum for session observation, tool result, user statement, human correction, execution receipt, outcome feedback, and imported seed. Add source revision, source event time, ingestion idempotency key, redaction receipt, safety classification, Work Request/execution provenance, and evidence digest. Evidence remains append-only.

Add these supporting tables:

- `memory_projection`: immutable L0 abstract, L1 overview, and L2 detail projections keyed by memory version, projection contract version, content digest, and token estimate. L2 points to bounded evidence detail; it does not copy a transcript.
- `memory_entity`: normalized entity links with type, canonical reference when known, confidence, and extractor revision.
- `memory_relation`: append-only typed relations for supports, duplicates, conflicts_with, supersedes, derived_from, corrects, and suppresses. Each relation names its decision basis and policy revision.
- `memory_consolidation_decision`: candidate, comparison set, proposed action, deterministic disposition, evidence thresholds, model proposal digest, deciding actor or job, and receipt.
- `memory_embedding`: a derived vector index keyed by memory version, projection level, embedding route, model revision, dimension, and content digest. It is rebuildable and never canonical content.
- `memory_retrieval_run` and `memory_retrieval_candidate`: query digest, server-derived scope, policy revision, signal scores, exclusions, selected projection level, token cost, rank, and final disposition.
- `memory_use_signal`: selected memory, consuming execution/session, intended use, downstream outcome reference, human feedback, miss/conflict code, and observed time.
- `memory_policy_revision`: immutable thresholds, weights, freshness rules, auto-promotion eligibility, quarantine rules, token budgets, and model/index revisions. Only an accepted administrative path activates a revision.

Enable pgvector in Neon only as a derived index inside the same database. If the vector route or extension is unavailable, recall degrades to structured filters, exact match, full-text search, trigram similarity, entities, time, confidence, and recency; it never fails open or consults another memory store.

## Evidence ingestion and safety

Add `observe-memory-evidence` as the primary machine-safe ingest verb. The caller may provide only the typed observation and stable source reference. Tenant, actor, sponsor, personal/shared visibility, agent principal, project, Work Request, plan, execution envelope, and run identity are resolved from authenticated server context and referenced ledgers. Caller-supplied identity or authority fields are rejected.

Idempotency binds tenant, source kind, source reference, source revision, evidence digest, and ingest contract version. Exact replay returns the prior receipt. Changed evidence appends a new row.

The safety classifier is fail-closed:

- Credentials, tokens, private keys, cookies, raw environment values, and high-entropy secrets are rejected and never embedded.
- Instructions that claim authority, attempt to alter system behavior, or originate in untrusted retrieved content are quarantined.
- Raw transcript bodies, unrestricted documents, and large tool payloads remain at their canonical source; memory stores only a bounded observation and locator.
- Client-sensitive facts require a declared sensitivity class and the same access boundary as their canonical source. V1 excludes regulated or highly sensitive client content from autonomous recall.
- Personal memory is visible only to the verified sponsor. Shared memory is tenant-scoped. Agent, project, and run scopes can narrow visibility but cannot widen it.

The quarantine read path is human-review only. Quarantined text is never returned by autonomous recall and never sent to the embedding adapter.

## Consolidation and promotion

Add a cognition contract `memory-candidate-extraction-v1` that returns a closed JSON schema: candidate kind, statement, bounded context, temporal bounds, entities, confidence, sensitivity, and proposed relations. Its database contract keeps `canonical_write_authority=false`.

Add a deterministic `consolidate-memory-candidate` job. It retrieves a bounded comparison set using exact digest, full-text/trigram similarity, entity overlap, temporal overlap, and—when available—vector similarity. It appends one decision:

- **supporting:** attach new evidence to the existing item when the normalized proposition and scope are identical;
- **duplicate:** record the duplicate relation and suppress the new candidate from recall;
- **conflicting:** keep both candidates non-autonomous and route a bounded review packet;
- **superseding:** propose a successor while preserving the prior row and validity interval;
- **new:** create a candidate with evidence and projections;
- **ignored or quarantined:** retain the receipt and reason without creating recallable memory.

V1 allows deterministic auto-promotion only for policy-allowlisted, low-sensitivity, non-authority memory types after multiple independent supporting observations or an exact authenticated human statement. Auto-promotion must name the active policy, threshold evidence, and job receipt. Procedural instructions, rules, permissions, commitments, client-sensitive facts, conflicts, and single-observation inferences always require human review. Human promotion, correction, and forgetting remain available and override autonomous eligibility.

Correction creates a successor and temporal closure; forgetting suppresses recall while preserving evidence and audit. A later model run cannot revive corrected or forgotten content without a new human-approved decision.

## Hybrid recall and progressive context

Replace the current full-text-only ranking with a two-stage bounded retrieval:

1. **Eligibility filter:** tenant, shared/personal owner, sponsor, agent, project, run, status, taint, sensitivity, temporal validity, source freshness, and optional entity constraints.
2. **Candidate fusion:** exact proposition/digest, PostgreSQL full-text rank, trigram similarity, vector similarity, entity overlap, temporal fit, confidence, corroboration count, recency, and prior-use quality.

Each signal is normalized to 0–1 under an immutable policy revision. Missing semantic vectors contribute zero and are identified as unavailable; weights are not silently redistributed. The response includes final score plus component scores, policy revision, exclusions, and evidence counts.

The context packer is deterministic. It receives a hard token budget, required scope, and intended task. It first selects diverse L0 abstracts, then upgrades only the highest-value items to L1, and uses L2 only when the caller explicitly requests evidence detail or a conflict requires inspection. It reserves budget for headings and citations, avoids redundant lineage members, and returns omitted counts and stop reasons. No model decides whether the budget was obeyed.

New read verbs:

- `recall-memory-v2`: ranked candidates and score provenance.
- `pack-memory-context`: final budgeted context with projection levels and evidence locators.
- `explain-memory-recall`: bounded audit view for why an item was selected, excluded, or outranked.
- Existing `recall-memory` remains compatible until consumers migrate, then becomes a wrapper over v2.

## Learning signals and evaluation

Every packed memory receives a stable retrieval-run reference. Consumers may append `record-memory-use` with intended use and a canonical outcome locator. Human feedback uses explicit helpful, incorrect, stale, irrelevant, missing, or unsafe labels. Tool receipts and accepted Work Request outcome feedback may supply deterministic success or failure signals.

Signals do not directly rewrite rank weights. An offline evaluation job compares candidate policy revisions against a versioned golden set containing positive queries, hard negatives, cross-tenant cases, personal/shared boundaries, stale facts, corrected/forgotten lineages, prompt injection, missing vectors, and token-budget edge cases. Promotion of a policy revision requires:

- no tenant or personal-scope leak;
- no quarantined or forgotten recall;
- zero authority-bearing instruction recall;
- minimum recall and ranking thresholds on the golden set;
- no regression beyond the accepted margin;
- deterministic packer replay;
- cost and latency within caps.

Initial metrics are recall@k, precision@k, MRR or nDCG, conflict surfacing rate, stale-memory rate, context utilization, citation coverage, p50/p95 latency, embedding backlog, quarantine count, and downstream helpfulness. These are evaluation evidence, not a claim that the agent has become correct.

## Runtime and observability

Use the existing `ops.job`, cognition contract, provider route, execution envelope, attempt receipt, and Engineering Passport infrastructure. Separate deterministic jobs for evidence normalization, consolidation, projection generation, embedding generation, and evaluation. Each job is idempotent, bounded, retryable, and emits a typed receipt.

Operational reads report candidate backlog, quarantine backlog, vector backlog by model revision, consolidation conflicts, stale projections, recall latency, zero-hit rate, safety exclusions, policy revision, eval score, and last successful first-use canary. Provider failure must leave canonical evidence intact and mark derived indexes stale or pending.

## Recovery and rollout

All schema changes are additive. Do not edit migration 0299 after it has shipped. Rollback disables new ingest/consolidation jobs and routes consumers back to the existing full-text recall wrapper. Append-only evidence, decisions, retrieval runs, and use signals remain for diagnosis. Derived projections and vectors can be rebuilt from canonical items and evidence.

Roll out in shadow mode:

1. Seed fixtures and enable pgvector on an isolated Neon branch.
2. Ingest synthetic session, tool, correction, and outcome evidence.
3. Prove idempotency, lineage, scope isolation, quarantine, and fail-closed behavior.
4. Compare v2 results with current recall without changing agent context.
5. Run the golden retrieval and safety suite.
6. Enable one canary consumer with a small token budget and explicit citations.
7. Deploy, migrate, read back schema and verbs, then prove one real agent session recalls a learned low-risk preference and records its outcome.
8. Keep autonomous promotion disabled for every non-allowlisted class until production evidence supports a policy revision.

## Engineering slices

1. **Schema and invariants:** additive migration, pgvector capability check, evidence types, server-derived scopes, safety classes, projections, relations, decisions, retrieval telemetry, grants, append-only triggers, and SQL negative fixtures.
2. **Safe evidence ingest:** `observe-memory-evidence`, redaction/quarantine, idempotency, source and execution anchors, and typed receipts.
3. **Candidate and consolidation path:** finite extraction contract, bounded comparison, explicit decisions, low-risk promotion policy, conflict review, correction and forgetting compatibility.
4. **Hybrid retrieval and packing:** derived embeddings, structured/full-text/trigram/vector/entity/temporal fusion, score provenance, progressive projections, deterministic budget packing, and compatibility wrapper.
5. **Learning signals and evaluation:** use/outcome feedback, golden set, offline policy comparison, safety and retrieval metrics, latency/cost telemetry.
6. **Shadow canary and first use:** isolated Neon rehearsal, migration proof, production readback, one canary agent workflow, rollback drill, and independent Engineering Passport review.

The capability is not operational until all eight Work Request acceptance criteria have evidence, the negative safety suite passes, the retrieval evaluation meets its accepted thresholds, production readback binds to the exact release, and one real agent use succeeds without a manual memory-file transfer.

# CARR Context & Learning Fabric — Heavy Build Master Plan

Historical status text corrected: WR-000013 has accepted immutable PLAN-d85ba97ccd46-v1. This current amended runbook is not itself a new accepted execution plan; no implementation authority is conferred.

## 1. Outcome

Build a Neon-native context and learning capability that lets every authorized CARR agent retain useful experience, recall the right evidence at the right time, and improve future work without allowing remembered content to become authority.

The finished capability is not merely long-term memory. It is a governed learning loop:

`experience -> evidence -> candidate knowledge -> governed activation -> bounded recall -> action -> measured outcome -> consolidation -> tested procedure`

Success means a future agent can use a prior preference, fact, correction, case, or proven procedure accurately; show where it came from; respect tenant, partner, project, and temporal boundaries; and improve measurable task performance over time.

## 2. Strategic crux

CARR already has a governed manual memory ledger and separate execution evidence. It does not yet have a closed, measurable loop that converts agent experience into evidence-bound, scoped, retrievable, and eventually procedural learning.

The crux is therefore not vector storage. Building only memory CRUD plus embeddings would improve recall but would not create learning. The essential system unit is the full loop from captured experience through outcome measurement and controlled procedural activation.

## 3. Research findings that bind the design

### Mem0

Adopt:

- write and read paths are separate;
- conversations are distilled into compact durable facts instead of replayed wholesale;
- additive history preserves temporal context;
- hybrid semantic, lexical, entity, and temporal signals outperform one search mode;
- retrieval and entity links are projections over durable memory records.

Do not copy:

- vector-store-first consistency or application-level race handling;
- opaque model decisions that mutate canonical memory;
- deletion or tenant-scope behavior that cannot be proven transactionally;
- vendor benchmark results as CARR acceptance criteria.

Current Mem0 V3 is materially different from its older ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP description: the current open-source prompt is additive and preserves old and new facts. That supports immutable history plus explicit supersession rather than destructive rewriting.

### OpenViking

Adopt:

- a unified address space for resources, memories, and skills;
- session commit and archive as a bounded asynchronous process;
- L0 abstract, L1 overview, and L2 evidence/detail;
- recursive, progressive retrieval that loads detail only when justified;
- a durable memory diff showing additions, updates, and retirements;
- typed memories that include events, cases, trajectories, experiences, tools, and skills.

Do not copy:

- filesystem content as the canonical truth;
- model-written file replacement as a memory update mechanism;
- vector indexes that can diverge from or strand canonical content;
- unbounded summary regeneration or retrieval prompts.

### Hermes

CARR will integrate through a standalone Hermes `MemoryProvider` bridge plus one generic Hermes framework correction described in Section 11. The bridge uses lifecycle hooks for bounded recall, turn synchronization, session end, pre-compression, session switching, and delegation. Hermes native `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` remain compatibility surfaces only until their duplicate-authority path is explicitly neutralized.

### Neon/PostgreSQL

Neon is the canonical store for records, evidence, memory state, context projections, embeddings, retrieval traces, outcomes, and policies. PostgreSQL transactions, constraints, grants, server-derived identity, mandatory FORCE RLS, and function-only runtime access provide the safety properties. `pgvector` is a derived search index inside the same database, not a second source of truth. Neon branches provide isolated migrations, evaluation, and recovery rehearsals.

### Practitioner evidence

Production reports consistently identify stale memories, duplication, silent overwrites, token growth, latency, weak tenant isolation, and inability to explain why a memory was or was not used. Therefore the system must make every write idempotent, every revision immutable, every retrieval reconstructible, every scope server-derived, every context pack bounded, and every deletion verifiable.

## 4. Complete target product

The finished product contains eight cooperating modules.

1. **Experience Ledger** — captures bounded, redacted, immutable session, turn, tool, correction, decision, and outcome evidence.
2. **Knowledge Compiler** — proposes typed memory candidates, detects support/duplicates/conflicts/supersession, and records every disposition.
3. **Context Catalog** — provides a unified database-native hierarchy for resources, memories, cases, and skills with L0/L1/L2 projections.
4. **Recall Engine** — performs authorization-first hybrid retrieval, optional reranking, progressive expansion, and exact score tracing.
5. **Context Packer** — assembles deterministic, token-bounded, source-cited context that treats all recalled content as untrusted context rather than instruction authority.
6. **Hermes Memory Bridge** — supplies bounded prefetch and explicit deeper-recall tools through the supported provider interface.
7. **Learning Lab** — links recalled context and agent actions to outcomes, proposes reusable procedures, evaluates them offline, and activates only accepted versions.
8. **Learning Control Room** — exposes candidates, conflicts, retrieval explanations, cost/latency/quality, deletion status, failed jobs, canaries, and rollback controls.

The Context Catalog and Context Packer are not a second context authority. CARR already has the active, plan-bound `context-bundle.v1` compiler and `activate-context-bundle` path. This build evolves that contract and implementation to `context-bundle.v2`, preserving accepted-plan binding, item digests, mode, expiry, activation receipt, and item-count limits while adding personal-scope compilation, hybrid retrieval provenance, progressive representations, and token accounting. During migration, v1 is a compatibility input to the single activation path; only one active binding may feed a run.

## 5. Non-deferrable commitments

1. Neon/PostgreSQL is canonical; files and embeddings are rebuildable projections.
2. Existing `memory_item` and `memory_evidence` are extended additively; migration 0299 is never rewritten.
3. Raw transcripts and unbounded tool payloads are not copied into memory. Durable evidence is typed, bounded, redacted, and source-referenced.
4. Every active memory has provenance, identity scope, temporal semantics, extractor/policy versions, and lifecycle lineage.
5. Tenant, sponsor, user, agent, project, work request, and session scope are derived server-side before retrieval or mutation.
6. Memory is context, never authority. It cannot grant permission, change doctrine, activate a rule, or authorize an action.
7. Model output can propose; deterministic policy and authorized humans decide canonical activation.
8. Every retrieval is reconstructible from eligible rows, component scores, policy version, model versions, and token decisions.
9. Corrections, forgetting, export, deletion, and restoration are first-class tested workflows.
10. The runtime must degrade safely when embeddings, rerankers, extractors, or network models are unavailable.
11. No broad rollout occurs before isolated rehearsal, shadow comparison, authenticated first use, independent verification, and a completed rollback drill.
12. Procedural learning does not activate until it has counterexamples, regression tests, scoped authority, and an accepted activation receipt.
13. Existing `policy-learning.v1` remains binding until a separately versioned, human-accepted learning-boundary contract replaces the relevant prohibition. No plan text or model output implicitly overrides it.

### Canonical versus derived data

Canonical:

- normalized experience/evidence events;
- memory items, evidence, lifecycle and temporal lineage;
- consolidation decisions;
- resource/skill identifiers and source revision bindings;
- retrieval policies;
- outcome and human-feedback signals;
- procedure/skill versions, evaluations, and activation receipts.

The memory lineage is event-sourced. `memory_item` remains the stable identity and compatibility/current projection. New immutable tables are canonical:

- `memory_assertion`: stable subject/predicate/value identity;
- `memory_revision`: typed value, unit, polarity, text projection, occurrence range, `[valid_from, valid_to)`, `observed_at`, append-only system sequence, extractor/prompt/model/policy versions;
- `memory_evidence_edge`: exact source revision/span, origin channel, role, quote depth, directness, sensitivity, and taint;
- `memory_state_event`: candidate, active, quarantined, forgotten, and deleted transitions;
- `memory_disposition_event`: supporting, duplicate, conflict, correction, supersession, rejection, and expiration decisions.

Runtime roles lose direct INSERT/UPDATE on `memory_item`; hardened functions append immutable rows and update the compatibility projection atomically. Existing rows receive migration-generated assertions, revisions, evidence bindings, and state events with preserved IDs and digests. Source directness, extractor confidence, and corroboration remain separate signals; the current single `confidence` scalar is never treated as all three.

Derived and rebuildable:

- embeddings;
- FTS/trigram materializations;
- entity co-occurrence links;
- L0/L1 summaries;
- denormalized current views;
- retrieval caches and aggregate metrics.
